applicability.scope: MLX evaluation/stream/buffer diagnosis at the pinned implementation; qualify the actual backend separately.
applicability.prerequisites: Access to the pinned MLX execution/lifetime contract and a bounded reproduction with an identified evaluation/read boundary; device-dependent conclusions need the actual selected backend.
applicability.input_contract: MLX revision/build, backend/device, Python/C++ entry, array shapes/dtypes, primitive streams, evaluation/read boundary and transformation context; timing needs warmup/work boundaries, while memory needs live references, in-flight buffers, allocator cache and synchronized observations.
applicability.produced_artifact: A producer/evaluation/dependency-wait/backend/availability-cleanup trace, ownership table, observed symptom and one discriminating check with build-bound actual evidence status.
applicability.failure_modes: Timing graph construction or submission as execution, assuming evaluated means completed, synchronizing only the default stream, or treating graph detachment/Python deletion as reusable storage can misdiagnose time or memory.
applicability.refusal_point: Stop when the trace answers the question; if the required backend is absent, retain the source-supported diagnosis and exact runtime gap rather than substituting CPU import success.

limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local native-backend, model, service or efficacy validation.
Static content checks do not promote this candidate or establish installed API conformance.
recommendations: Separate graph construction, async_eval submission, eval and host reads, and record which stream the measurement actually synchronizes.
Preserve the dependency-wait path and selected backend buffer-retention/donation contract before changing streams or assuming storage can be reused.
Distinguish live, in-flight and allocator-cached memory; inspect the real error/cleanup path before proposing a leak fix or hiding the failure.
